scientific_findings.finding: For the stated symmetric positive-definite A and budget-only constraint, x=(1/7,3/7) and w=(1/4,3/4). The modeled variance is 7/4 percentage-points squared, or 7/40000 in fractional-return units. The 12.5 percent reduction is within the supplied covariance model.

The ideal state is (|0>+3|1>)/sqrt(10), with probabilities (1/10,9/10). The probabilities used as weights give variance 46/25. Square roots recover the ratio only with known positive components; signed real solutions require relative-sign information. The allocations here do not require the solution's absolute norm.

A+I minimizes w^T A w + ||w||_2^2 under the same budget constraint and produces weights (1/3,2/3). Their variance under the original covariance is 16/9, exceeding 7/4 by 1/36 or 1/63 relatively. Both solvers must solve the same objective when their performance is compared.

The illustrative sequential total is 75 seconds and exceeds the 60-second target. A 90-second measured p95 and a 75-second hypothetical sum do not establish a measured speedup. The p95, per-weight error, budget residual, excess modeled variance and failures must be evaluated consistently. The exercise's thresholds are educational choices.
